messages:
oncall-bot: Heads-up: planned maintenance window for control-plane routing tomorrow 2026-03-18 03:00–05:00 UTC. Expected rolling restarts of router pods; short <1m 502/500 spikes possible. Status page draft -> https://status.redwood.example/ops/maintenance-3345678901 :warning:

sara_ops: Can we move it to 03:00-05:00 UTC instead of 02:00-04:00 to avoid EU morning traffic? cc @mike_sre

mike_sre: 03:00-05:00 works for infra. We'll need an extra hand for live drain/fallback 03:30–04:30. I'll take primary oncall for the window, will do handoff notes.

jess_prod: Need enterprise customer notice copy (SLA, rollback timeframe, contact). Also include that Dedicated customers can opt into a surge-protection mode to cap throughput during the window.

nate_support: Drafted a short customer blurb, dropping here for quick review:
```
We will perform maintenance on our control plane on 2026-03-18 from 03:00–05:00 UTC. You may observe brief request errors or slightly elevated latency. No action needed; most traffic will fail-over automatically. If you have strict SLAs, reply and we'll schedule a dedicated bypass. Contact: support@redwood.example or +1-555-0202.
```

sara_ops: Add: "Automatic fallback to model-variant small/quantized will be active for hosted API routes; customers using Dedicated with pinned routing will be notified individually."

mike_sre: Ops playbook for the window (short):
1) 02:50 — preflight checks, confirm KV-cache health and replica counts
2) 03:00 — start controlled rolling restart (region-by-region, north-america then europe)
3) 03:30 — enable traffic shaping + model-variant fallback if tail error >0.5%
4) 03:45 — simulate rollback in staging for 5m (no prod changes)
5) 04:30 — re-evaluate, finish remainder of restarts
6) 05:00 — validation and close
I'll paste the runbook link to the bridge in a bit.

jess_prod: For the customer-facing status page, use: "We expect short intermittent errors and elevated latency. No data loss expected. If your app requires stricter latency, see our dedicated bypass options." Keep it plain language.

legal_review: Quick flag: add one sentence about "planned maintenance" not constituting an SLA breach unless prolonged. Sending approved wording now.

nate_support: Legal text added and bulletin scheduled for 12:00 UTC today to go to affected enterprise contacts. I'll also pin a copy in #customer-notify when ready.

oncall-bot: Reminder schedule set: 24h before (3345592501) and 1h before (3345675301). Auto-post to #statuspage and notify @oncall rotation.

sara_ops: Thanks everyone — tagging @mike_sre for the handoff: please post your handoff snippet 15m before start and confirm the bridge URL. :thumbsup:

mike_sre: Will do. Bridge: https://meet.redwood.example/bridge/3345678901. Handoff snippet to post at 02:45: "mike_sre: primary oncall for maintenance window 03:00–05:00 UTC; sara_ops secondary; contact via bridge. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood.example/runbooks/ctrlplane-maint"

nate_support: Once Mike posts handoff I'll run the customer broadcast and attach the statuspage draft.

sara_ops: Added an internal escalation template for support to use if customers query SLA impact: "If customers report >5% request failure for >10m escalate immediately to oncall with priority alert and page SRE leads."

mike_sre: Confirmed. Will perform the staging rollback test at 03:45 and report results in-bridge.

oncall-bot: Maintenance notice posted to #statuspage and scheduled email blast to enterprise contacts at 12:00 UTC.

sara_ops: Closing checklist: preflight run 02:50, handoff posted 02:45, bridge live 02:55. See you all on the bridge. :white_check_mark:
